docs.title: Endpoint 2: Biela Model Calculation
docs.text:
@app.post("/api/analytical/biela")
async def calculate_biela(request: BielaModelRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]

Purpose: Calculate switching losses using Biela analytical model

Request: 

{
  "c_oss": 150e-12,
  "q_g": 50e-9,
  "v_plateau": 5.0,
  "r_g_on": 10.0,
  "r_g_off": 10.0,
  "v_dc": 400.0,
  "i_load": 20.0,
  "t_j": 25.0,
  "i_min": 0,
  "i_max": 50,
  "i_points": 50
}

Response: 

{
  "operating_point": {
    "v_dc": 400.0,
    "i_load": 20.0,
    "t_j": 25.0
  },
  "results": {
    "e_on": 0.000123,
    "e_off": 0.000087,
    "e_total": 0.000210
  },
  "curve": {
    "currents": [0, 1.02, 2.04, ..., 50],
    "e_on": [0, 6.3e-6, 1.25e-5, ..., 3.1e-4],
    "e_off": [0, 4.5e-6, 8.9e-5, ..., 2.2e-4],
    "e_total": [0, 1.08e-5, 2.14e-5, ..., 5.3e-4]
  }
}

Features: - Single operating point calculation (E_on, E_off, E_total) - Optional curve generation over current range - Temperature compensation (+0.3%/K above 25°C) - Energy values in Joules (frontend converts to µJ)

Physics-Based Model: 1. Turn-On Energy: E_on = 0.5 × V_dc × I_load × (t_ri + t_fv) + 0.5 × C_oss × V_dc² - t_ri: Current rise time (gate charging through Miller plateau) - t_fv: Voltage fall time (C_oss discharge) 2. Turn-Off Energy: E_off = 0.5 × V_dc × I_load × (t_rv + t_fi) - t_rv: Voltage rise time (C_oss charging) - t_fi: Current fall time (gate discharging)

docs.title: Endpoint 3: Gate Charge Model Calculation
docs.text:
@app.post("/api/analytical/gate_charge")
async def calculate_gate_charge(request: GateChargeModelRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]

Purpose: Calculate switching times using gate charge model

Request: 

{
  "q_gs": 10e-9,
  "q_gd": 15e-9,
  "q_g": 50e-9,
  "v_th": 2.5,
  "v_plateau": 5.0,
  "r_g": 10.0,
  "r_g_int": 1.0,
  "v_driver": 15.0,
  "v_off": 0.0
}

Response: 

{
  "parameters": {
    "q_gs": 1e-8,
    "q_gd": 1.5e-8,
    "q_g": 5e-8,
    "v_th": 2.5,
    "v_plateau": 5.0,
    "r_g_total": 11.0
  },
  "turn_on_times": {
    "t_delay": 15.3,
    "t_rise": 8.7,
    "t_fall_v": 27.5,
    "t_total": 51.5
  },
  "turn_off_times": {
    "t_delay": 12.8,
    "t_rise_v": 33.0,
    "t_fall_i": 6.7,
    "t_total": 52.5
  }
}

Features: - All times in nanoseconds (converted from seconds in backend) - Separate turn-on and turn-off timing analysis - Breakdown into delay, rise/fall phases - Total transition time for each direction

Model Equations: - Turn-On Delay: t_d = R_g × Q_gs × ln(V_driver / (V_driver - V_th)) - Current Rise: t_ri = R_g × Q_rise / (V_driver - V_plateau) - Voltage Fall: t_fv = R_g × Q_gd / (V_driver - V_plateau)

docs.title: Endpoint 4: DPT Netlist Generation
docs.text:
@app.post("/api/dpt/generate_netlist")
async def generate_dpt_netlist(transistor_id: str, config: DPTConfigRequest) -> Dict[str, str]

Purpose: Generate LTspice Double Pulse Test netlist for a transistor

Request: 

{
  "transistor_id": "IPW60R045CP",
  "config": {
    "v_dc": 400.0,
    "i_target": 20.0,
    "l_load": 100e-6,
    "r_g_on": 10.0,
    "r_g_off": 10.0,
    "v_g_on": 15.0,
    "v_g_off": -5.0,
    "t_dead": 5e-6,
    "t_pulse2": 2e-6
  }
}

Response: 

{
  "netlist": "Version 4\nSHEET 1 880 680\n...",
  "transistor_name": "IPW60R045CP",
  "config": {
    "v_dc": 400.0,
    "i_target": 20.0,
    "r_g_on": 10.0,
    "r_g_off": 10.0
  }
}

Features: - Full LTspice .asc netlist format - Double pulse waveform generation - Load inductance sizing (first pulse duration calculated to reach target current) - Gate driver circuit with configurable resistances - Measurement probes for V_ds, I_d, V_gs

Circuit Topology: 

V_dc --+-- DUT (Switch) --+-- Load Inductor (L_load) -- GND
       |                  |
       +-- Freewheeling Diode

Gate Driver: V_on/V_off with R_g_on/R_g_off
Pulse 1: Charge inductor to I_target
Dead Time: 5 µs
Pulse 2: Turn-off transient (measure E_off)

@app.post("/api/transistors/{transistor_id}/dpt_validate")
async def validate_dpt_data(transistor_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]

Purpose: Validate DPT measurement data against datasheet specifications

Response: 

{

  ],
  "warnings": [

Use Cases: - Identify test conditions that violate ratings - Detect datasheet inconsistencies - Verify measurement data quality before export

docs.text:
Added 6 new API methods to TransistorAPI class:

// PLECS Import
async importPLECS(file) {
  const formData = new FormData()
  formData.append('file', file)
  const response = await api.post('/api/import/plecs', formData, {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data' }
  })
  return response.data
}

// Analytical Models
async calculateBiela(params) {
  const response = await api.post('/api/analytical/biela', params)
  return response.data
}

async calculateGateCharge(params) {
  const response = await api.post('/api/analytical/gate_charge', params)
  return response.data
}

// DPT (Double Pulse Test)
async generateDPTNetlist(transistorId, config) {
  const response = await api.post('/api/dpt/generate_netlist', config, {
    params: { transistor_id: transistorId }
  })
  return response.data
}

async getDPTData(transistorId) {
  const response = await api.get(`/api/transistors/${transistorId}/dpt_data`)
  return response.data
}

async validateDPTData(transistorId) {
  const response = await api.post(`/api/transistors/${transistorId}/dpt_validate`)
  return response.data
}

docs.title: State Management
docs.text:
const files = ref([])           // Array of FileItem objects
const importing = ref(false)    // Import in progress flag
const importResults = ref([])   // Array of PLECSImportResponse objects

// Computed properties
const pendingCount = computed(() =>
  files.value.filter(f => f.status === 'pending').length
)
const totalImported = computed(() =>
  importResults.value.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.transistors_imported, 0)
)
const allImportedIds = computed(() => {
  const ids = []
  importResults.value.forEach(r => ids.push(...r.transistor_ids))
  return ids
})

docs.title: Import Flow
docs.text:
1. User uploads files → addFiles() validates size, adds to queue
  2. User clicks Import → startImport() processes sequentially
  3. For each file:
  4. Set status to 'uploading'
  5. Call transistorApi.importPLECS(file)
  6. Update status to 'success' or 'error'
  7. Store result in importResults
  8. Emit 'import-complete' event with total count and IDs

}

docs.title: Key Functions
docs.text:
async function loadDPTData() {
  dptData.value = await transistorApi.getDPTData(selectedTransistorId.value)
}

async function generateNetlist() {
  generating.value = true
  generatedNetlist.value = await transistorApi.generateDPTNetlist(
    selectedTransistorId.value,
    dptConfig.value
  )
  generating.value = false
}

async function validateData() {
  validating.value = true
  validationResults.value = await transistorApi.validateDPTData(
    selectedTransistorId.value
  )
  validating.value = false
}

function copyNetlist() {
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(generatedNetlist.value.netlist)
  alert('Netlist copied to clipboard!')
}

function downloadNetlist() {
  const blob = new Blob([generatedNetlist.value.netlist], { type: 'text/plain' })
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob)
  const link = document.createElement('a')
  link.href = url
  link.download = `${generatedNetlist.value.transistor_name}_DPT.asc`
  link.click()
}

docs.title: Backend Limitations
docs.text:
1. PLECS Import:
  2. Limited to XML format (no binary .plecs files)
  3. Some PLECS-specific metadata not preserved

  4. Thermal model conversion may lose precision

  5. Analytical Models:

  6. Biela model assumes inductive switching (not valid for capacitive loads)
  7. Gate charge model ignores parasitic inductances

  8. IGBT model not yet implemented in web interface

  9. DPT Netlist:

  10. Requires PyLTSpice for simulation (not included in web backend)
  11. No automatic waveform analysis (manual inspection required)
  12. Single device only (no half-bridge support)

docs.title: Frontend Limitations

  8. No zoom/pan persistence across tab switches

  9. Validation:

  10. DPT validation rules hardcoded (not user-configurable)
  11. No comparison to industry standards (IEC, MIL-STD)
  12. No automated test report generation

"""Test for memory leaks in GUI."""
import pytest
import gc
import sys
from pytestqt.qtbot import QtBot
from transistordatabase.gui.gui import MainWindow


def test_repeated_window_creation_no_leak(qtbot):
    """Test that creating/destroying windows doesn't leak memory."""
    import psutil
    import os

    process = psutil.Process(os.getpid())
    initial_memory = process.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024  # MB

    # Create and destroy 10 windows
    for i in range(10):
        window = MainWindow()
        qtbot.addWidget(window)
        window.show()
        qtbot.wait(100)
        window.close()
        window.deleteLater()

        # Force garbage collection
        gc.collect()
        qtbot.wait(100)

    final_memory = process.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024  # MB
    memory_increase = final_memory - initial_memory

    # Memory should not increase by more than 50 MB
    assert memory_increase < 50, f"Memory increased by {memory_increase} MB (expected < 50 MB)"


def test_plot_generation_no_leak(qtbot):
    """Test that generating plots repeatedly doesn't leak."""
    window = MainWindow()
    qtbot.addWidget(window)

    import psutil

    process = psutil.Process(os.getpid())

    # Generate plots 20 times

        # Trigger plot generation (implementation-specific)

        gc.collect()

docs.title: Core Principle
docs.text:
Switching loss is a commutation-system phenomenon, not a datasheet scalar.

Every entry in the database represents a switching pair — the minimum unit of a converter leg. A "single device" is the special case where both sides are the same device (standard DPT assumption).

docs.title: Single Unified Database
docs.text:
transistordatabase/switching_pairs/
├── Cree_C3M0075120K.json                              # Self-pair (datasheet)
├── Infineon_IPW65R048CFDA.json                         # Self-pair (datasheet)
├── Infineon_IPW65R048CFDA__ST_STTH30RQ06DY.json        # MOS + external diode
├── Infineon_IPW65R080CFDA__Infineon_IPW65R080CFDA.json # MOS + MOS (half-bridge)
├── 10x_ST_SCTW100N65G2AG.json                          # 10 parallel (self-pair)
└── ...

One JSON file per switching pair. Git-friendly, easy diffs, clear ownership.

File naming convention: {high_side}__{low_side}.json (double underscore separator) - Self-pair: just {device_id}.json - Parallel: {N}x_{device_id}.json or {N}x_{device_id}__{M}x_{device_id2}.json

docs.title: .mat Filename Parsing Rules
docs.text:
Pattern                                    Action
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Vendor_PartNumber.mat                     → Self-pair (base device)
Vendor_PartNumber1_with_Vendor_PN2.mat    → Combination pair (MIGRATE)
Vendor_PN1_with_SiC_Diode.mat            → SKIP (2nd P/N unclear)
N_x_Vendor_PartNumber.mat                → Parallel self-pair
Vendor_PN_125C.mat                        → MERGE into base device temp array
Vendor_PN_Eon.mat                         → MERGE into base device E_on data
Vendor_PN_Eoff.mat                        → MERGE into base device E_off data
Vendor_PN_Vfwd.mat                        → MERGE into base device conduction data
Vendor_PN_Vrev.mat                        → MERGE into base device reverse conduction

  3. Extract per-device:

  5. Turn-on/off energy LUT (current × voltage × temperature → energy)
  6. Thermal RC model (Foster/Cauer elements)
  7. Analytical formulas (if present)

  8. Metadata (vendor, partnumber, class)

    import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

PLECS_NS = 'http://www.plexim.com/xml/semiconductors/'

def parse_plecs_xml(xml_path):
    tree = ET.parse(xml_path)
    root = tree.getroot()
    ns = {'p': PLECS_NS}

    package = root.find('.//p:Package', ns)
    vendor = package.get('vendor', '')
    partnumber = package.get('partnumber', '')
    device_class = package.get('class', '')

    # Extract switching energy tables
    turn_on = extract_energy_table(package, 'TurnOnLoss', ns)
    turn_off = extract_energy_table(package, 'TurnOffLoss', ns)
    conduction = extract_conduction_table(package, ns)
    thermal = extract_thermal_model(package, ns)

    return {
        'vendor': vendor,
        'partnumber': partnumber,
        'device_class': device_class,
        'turn_on': turn_on,
        'turn_off': turn_off,
        'conduction': conduction,
        'thermal': thermal
    }

│   ├── source: str (datasheet, dpt_measurement, etc.)
│   ├── turn_on: SwitchingEnergyData
│   ├── turn_off: SwitchingEnergyData

docs.title: Mixin-Based GUI Design
docs.text:
The PyQt5 GUI employs a modular mixin-based architecture that provides:

Benefits: 1. Modularity - Each mixin is a separate concern 2. Testability - Mixins can be tested independently 3. Maintainability - Code is organized by functionality 4. Scalability - New features added as new mixins 5. Reusability - Mixins can be composed with other classes

File Structure: 

transistordatabase/gui/
├── gui.py (950 LOC) - MainWindow class
├── _widgets.py - Reusable widgets
├── _utils.py - Utility functions
├── api_client.py - REST API client
└── mixins/ (5,957 LOC)
    ├── utils_mixin.py (UtilitiesMixin)
    ├── settings_mixin.py (SettingsMixin)
    ├── search_mixin.py (SearchDatabaseMixin)
    ├── creation_mixin.py (TransistorCreationMixin)
    ├── curve_mixin.py (CurveManagementMixin)
    ├── export_mixin.py (ExportToolsMixin)
    ├── comparison_mixin.py (ComparisonToolsMixin)
    └── topology_mixin.py (TopologyCalculatorMixin)

docs.text:
Port Mismatch Between Frontend and Backend

  • Frontend Configuration (src/services/api.js line 8): Configured to call API at http://localhost:8002

  • Backend Running On: Was incorrectly running on http://localhost:8000 (wrong port!)

  • Result: Frontend made API calls to port 8002, but no server was listening there. Backend on port 8000 had the data but frontend couldn't reach it.

docs.title: 1. Backend Was Healthy (Port 8000)
docs.text:
$ curl http://localhost:8000/api/transistors
# Returned 25 transistors successfully ✅

docs.title: 2. Frontend Configuration (api.js)
docs.text:
// Line 8 in src/services/api.js
return 'http://localhost:8002'  // Frontend expects port 8002

docs.title: 3. Documentation Confirms Port 8002
docs.text:
• README_updated.rst: Documents API at http://localhost:8002
  • tests/README.md: Backend should run on port 8002
  • tests/quick_test.sh: Kills processes on port 8002

docs.title: Step 1: Stop Backend on Wrong Port
docs.text: kill -9 $(lsof -ti:8000)

docs.title: Step 2: Restart Backend on Correct Port
docs.text:
cd /home/tinix/claude_wsl/transistordatabase
uv run uvicorn transistordatabase.gui_web.backend.main:app --port 8002 --reload

docs.title: Step 3: Verification
docs.text:
# Server Status:
✅ Vue dev server: RUNNING on port 5173
✅ FastAPI backend: RUNNING on port 8002
✅ Old port 8000: correctly stopped

# API Test:

✅ Returns 25 transistors

docs.title: Debug Checklist
docs.text:
1. Check Server Status 

    # Both should show processes running
lsof -i:5173  # Vue dev server
lsof -i:8002  # FastAPI backend

  2. Test API Directly 

    curl http://localhost:8002/api/transistors | head -c 500
# Should return JSON starting with: [{"metadata":{"name":"Fuji_...

  3. Check Browser Console Press F12, go to Console tab. Look for errors mentioning:

docs.title: Loading a Transistor
docs.text:
from transistordatabase import DatabaseManager

# Initialize database
db = DatabaseManager()

# Load a transistor
transistor = db.load_transistor("C2M0080120D")

# Access properties
print(f"Name: {transistor.metadata.name}")
print(f"Type: {transistor.metadata.type}")
print(f"Manufacturer: {transistor.metadata.manufacturer}")
print(f"Max Voltage: {transistor.electrical_ratings.v_abs_max} V")
print(f"Max Current: {transistor.electrical_ratings.i_abs_max} A")

docs.title: Using Analytical Models
docs.text:
from transistordatabase.analytical_models import ChristenBielaModel, HalfBridgeParams

# Create model from transistor data
model = ChristenBielaModel.from_transistor(transistor)

# Calculate switching energy
params = HalfBridgeParams(
    v_0=600,      # DC bus voltage (V)
    i_0=20,       # Load current (A)
    v_g_on=20,    # Gate-on voltage (V)
    v_g_off=-5,   # Gate-off voltage (V)
    r_g=10        # Gate resistance (Ω)
)

result = model.calc_switching_energy(params)
print(f"Turn-on energy: {result.e_on*1e6:.2f} µJ")
print(f"Turn-off energy: {result.e_off*1e6:.2f} µJ")

docs.title: Exporting to Simulation Tools
docs.text:
from transistordatabase.backend.concrete_services import ConcreteServiceFactory

# Create export service
factory = ConcreteServiceFactory()
exporter = factory.create_export_service()

# Export to PLECS
from pathlib import Path
exporter.export_to_plecs(transistor, Path("transistor.xml"))

# Export to GeckoCIRCUITS
export_params = {"working_directory": "output/"}
exporter.export_to_gecko_circuits(transistor, export_params)
